name: Rancher Rambo | Chapter 2 Starter Guide
description_md:
Rancher Rambo

>This series provides 10 playtested decks using the Chapter 2 Core and new Starters, with each deck compatible for two player with at least 7 others (and working well at high player counts). Using his trusty [Knapsack](/card/60552), Miguel lays fast traps like [Lie in Wait](/card/60566) or [Glassing](/card/60563) one location away and then drags enemies into them with [Loner](/card/60557). For any foes that survive the trip, this rancher Rambo uses [Longbow](/card/60580) to finish them off. `If you want to support my work, give it a like ❤︎ and a favorite ★ on here!`

Series Decks

|   Mystic   |   Rogue   |   Guardian   |   Survivor   |   Seeker   | |:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:|:---:| | Marie | André | Tommy| Miguel | Carolyn | | Dexter | Trish | Daniela | Izzie | Joe |

At a Glance

>| Stats | | >|:---|:---| >| Clue-finding: |  ★★★☆☆ | >| Consistency: |  ★★★☆☆ | >| Enemy Management: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Encounter Defense: |  ★★★★★ | >| Survivability: |  ★★★★☆ | >| Simplicity: |  ★★☆☆☆ |

Overview

- They struck first blood: The goal of this deck is to lay a trap at an adjacent locations (either with [Knapsack](/card/60552), or place and move away), and then drag engaged enemies as a action to the trapped empty location with [Loner](/card/60557). Doing this allows you to investigate using with [Glassing](/card/60563), or kill stuff with [Lie in Wait](/card/60566) (or [Makeshift Bomb](/card/60581) if you're feeling reckless). [Longbow](/card/60580) is there as a finisher, with the added benefit of targeting Aloof enemies without engaging. You can also place traps on choke point locations which Hunters will move through, or you can scare the [Feline Hybrid](/card/60553) with a fight action to trigger a cleverly placed Glassing too. The world is your oyster! - The (Mutant) Deer Hunter: To support the above, [Stalk Prey](/card/60567) allows you to spawn enemies with Miguel's free event action - getting a clue and a card in the bargain. In classic survivor fashion upgraded [Hunter's Instinct](/card/60574) and [Do-or-Die](/card/60568) give you options to recur events such as your traps or Stalk Prey. Notably, [Scrape By](/card/12082) can be recovered too - which is very nice for clue-finding with Stalk Prey (investigate, pass with Scrape By, spawn an enemy in with Stalk Prey, recur Scrape By - netting you two clues unless you draw on the investigate). There were turns where I both got 3 clues using this method and killed the 3 health enemy with [Longbow](/card/60580) (investigate, event, attack, investigate) - pretty sweet! - Even more hunting: [Guerrilla Tactics](/card/60576) allows you to snipe enemies from a distance (especially those that have triggered a damage trap), and is made even better with [Loner](/card/60557) to close ground. ["Shove off!"](/card/12079) means you don't have to choose between evading and damage when you don't want to. [Daniel Jameson](/card/60555) is there so you can have a redo on fighting and evading, making you extremely consistent in this regard while also boosting your stat. This includes fight attempts on Guerrilla Tactics or [Lie in Wait](/card/60566). A fun interaction on the latter is for Elusive Hunter enemies (e.g. [Bat Horror](/card/12162)) while you're at the trap's location: they move in during the enemy phase, they engage with you (and trigger [Hunter's Instinct](/card/60574)) but Lie in Wait's triggers before they make their attack - and so due to Elusive they get scared off (even if you fail the attack). - The survival instinct: While this deck isn't especially strong in any one area, it's not overly weak in any either. The deck has 17 icons to help with a wide range of tests, and when you inevitably fail some then [Rabbit's Foot](/card/60560) allows you to draw cards in the bargain - with [Scrape By](/card/12082) giving a do-over on fails. With the icons and Scrape By, I gave Encounter Defense a 5 ★ rating. While the only soak here is [Daniel Jameson](/card/60555) or your [Knapsack](/card/60552), Miguel's thic 8/8 sanity and health mean you need less soak than other investigators. The Knapsack can also provide card draw if you need it. - Resource generation: [Same Old Thing](/card/60561) is a psuedo-[Emergency Cache](/card/12089) for events (and can fund other investigators' events as well). Speaking of E-cache, you can recur this with [Hunter's Instinct](/card/60574) and use your extra action to play it. While there's likely better things you'll want to recur, it's nice to know you can if you're cash-strapped! Thank you: [5argon](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/61394/5argon) and [their thumbnail tool](https://arkham-starter.com/tool/thumbnails); [Valentin1331](https://arkhamdb.com/user/profile/42890/Valentin1331) for his support over the years; the community creators of [Arkham.Build](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhambuild/) ([Felix](https://spoettel.dev/)), [Arkham Cards](https://www.patreon.com/c/arkhamcards/) ([zzorba](https://www.reddit.com/user/zzorba/)) and [ArkhamDB](https://www.patreon.com/c/kamalisk/) ([kamalisk](https://www.reddit.com/user/kamalisk/)) - linking their Patreons!

Explain Yourself!

I think this deck isn't too surprising for Miguel - it packs some non-fast events which use his ability and can also be recurred through [Hunter's Instinct](/card/60574) and [Do-or-Die](/card/60568). I've heard people have struggled with enough non-fast events on Miguel for his ability to feel worth while, however the 9 eligible targets here feel appropriate in IMHO. For traps [Decoy Trap](/card/60562) is missing, but for me it's the most situational. The deck doesn't have much soak, but Miguel is a stout geezer so I don't think you need it. [Timely Intervention](/card/12081) sits in Izzie's deck (the level 0 version and then later the [upgraded version](/card/60582)). Realistically the level 0 version is just okay here, as Miguel has a whole lot of wilds to commit to tests and then [Rabbit's Foot](/card/60560) or his [Knapsack](/card/60552) to draw these. Additionally he has [Daniel](/card/60555) to retake fight and evade tests - including [Longbow](/card/60580) fight actions (dramatically reducing the need to have Timely Intervention to commit to these). This leaves treacheries or failures by 1 as the main use cases for Timely Intervention, which [Scrape By](/card/12082) already mitigates against. I bumped this deck up to a 3 ★ rating in clue-finding on a playtest. The [Scrape By](/card/12082) and [Stalk Prey](/card/60567) combo with [Hunter's Instinct](/card/60574) is pretty tasty, and your card draw is strong enough that you can usually assemble this engine. Plus, [Glassing](/card/60563) isn't half bad - a bit fiddly but as it provides a investigate it's essentially giving you action-less clue-finding. You can put it on a mid-shroud location while you bust a high shroud location with the Stalk Prey/Scrape By combo. Regarding other options, ["Look what I found!"](/card/12078) is absent as Miguel will fairly often fail by more than 2 on basic investigates - it's too situational.

Campaign starter and planned progression

0 XP deck is below (and link here): A recommended order of purchases/upgrades is: - [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094) → [Scrape By](/card/12082) - [Pocketknife](/card/60559) → [Longbow](/card/60580) - [Hunter's Instinct](/card/12074) → [Hunter's Instinct ••](/card/60574) - [Guerrilla Tactics](/card/60564) → [Guerrilla Tactics ••](/card/60576) - 1 x [Manual Dexterity](/card/12091) → 1 x [Makeshift Bomb](/card/60581) Post-19 XP suggestions are: - 1 x [Manual Dexterity](/card/12091) → 1 x [Makeshift Bomb](/card/60581) - ["Shove off!"](/card/12079) → [Rope Trap](/card/60578) - 1 x [Levelheaded •••](/card/60579) if you feel a need (though [Rabbit's Foot](/card/60560) or [Do-or-Die](/card/60568) are all that should be replaced)

Compatability Matrix

Everyone likes a good matrix! Below are all the decks that are compatible at two player using one Chapter 2 Core and one 2026 Starter Deck set: For higher player counts I've not 'compatabilized' the basic skills ([Overpower](/card/12092), [Manual Dexterity](/card/12091), [Guts](/card/12090), [Perception](/card/12093) and [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094)). There are only 4 copies of each in the Chapter 2 core, enough for any two decks. If playing 3+ players and there's a clash, you can either: - Swap with an appropriate level 0 class skill which that deck can use (e.g. [On the Brink](/card/60569) for [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094)). - Swap with a class event or asset with matching or similar symbols (e.g. [Working a Hunch](/card/12038) for [Perception](/card/12093)). - Swap with a different underused basic skill you still believe would be useful for the deck (e.g. [Guts](/card/12090) for [Unexpected Courage](/card/12094)). - Proxy however you see fit (especially if you own Chapter 1 cards, just use the old school versions and remember the slight difference around who draws the card). I empower you to do sensible things!

Final thoughts

Miguel is a weird guy! I didn't expect FFG to make the evergreen starter Survivor into a trapper, but I kind of like it (but equally, he almost feels like you're playing your own game within the game). Honestly I don't know whether Miguel should have a 5 ★ enemy management score, but he is perhaps less good at boss-killing than more conventional damage dealers. That said there's few people who can harass distant enemies quite so well, and the auto-damage with [Makeshift Bomb](/card/60581) can be very helpful. Add in other weird flavor here - like that the [Feline Hybrid](/card/60553) is somewhat helpful to trigger [Glassing](/card/60563) - and Miguel's playstyle feels unique. I dig it, it definitely swings for the fences in terms of quirky design! Any thoughts - drop them below!
